title: Ricotta and Mozzarella Calzones with Garlic Chilli Oil and Oregano
changes_from_base: The filling becomes ricotta, fresh mozzarella and parmesan bound with an egg yolk and seasoned with a gently cooked garlic and chilli oil and fresh oregano, with no spinach, and six calzones are baked in two batches on a hot stone.
summary: Six pillowy baked pastries with a luxurious filling of creamy ricotta, mozzarella and parmesan perfumed with warm garlic oil.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook or food processor
pizza peel or rimless baking sheet

ingredients.item: strong white bread flour, plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh mozzarella, grated or finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix dough
steps.text: Whisk the strong white bread flour, fast-action yeast and salt together in the mixer bowl, then with the hook turning on medium-low, pour in the olive oil and add the warm water gradually, mixing constantly for about 10 min until you reach a smooth, elastic dough (alternatively pulse in a food processor and knead briefly by hand).

steps.title: Bulk ferment
steps.text: Shape into a ball, place in a lightly oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for 1½–2 hours until the dough has roughly doubled.

steps.title: Infuse oil
steps.text: While the dough rises, warm the crushed garlic, olive oil and dried chilli flakes gently in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1½–2 min, just until sizzling and fragrant (reaching about 93 °C), tip into a bowl and cool for 10 min.

steps.title: Mix filling
steps.text: Stir together the ricotta, finely chopped or grated fresh mozzarella, finely grated parmesan, egg yolk, chopped fresh oregano, salt, black pepper and the cooled garlic oil, then cover and chill until needed.

steps.title: Final prep
steps.text: Put the pizza stone on the lowest shelf and heat the oven to 260 °C, line a tray with lightly oiled baking paper.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Turn the risen dough onto an unfloured work surface, cut into 6 equal pieces, shape each into a tight ball, cover and leave to rest for 15–30 min.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Cut 8 squares of baking paper about 23 cm across, roll each dough ball to a 23 cm circle and stack them in pairs with paper between, spread a sixth of the filling over half of each circle leaving a 2–3 cm border, fold over and press, then roll and crimp the edges firmly to seal, cut two small slits in each top, brush generously with olive oil and sprinkle with flaky sea salt.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Trim the baking paper, slide 3 calzones on their paper onto the hot stone and bake for about 11 min until golden, cool on a wire rack for 5 min, peel away the paper and serve; bake the second batch while the first cools.

tips: Infuse the oil slowly and gently so the garlic turns fragrant without browning or turning bitter.
Stack the dough circles with baking paper between them so they stay separate and don't stick together while resting.
Slide the paper-lined calzones directly onto the hot stone using a pizza peel, which gets them straight into the heat for maximum oven spring.
storage: Serve warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
